newsitem.title: USA: Dlr supported at U.S. open, then dips on PPI fall.
newsitem.headline: Dlr supported at U.S. open, then dips on PPI fall.

text.p: The dollar opened a touch higher versus the mark and yen after digesting the week's wild swings in a relatively calm overnight session, dealers said.

But the greenback softened somewhat after data showed U.S. producer price inflation was surprisingly tame in May. Dealers said they would settle in to wait for Wall Street's reaction, after Thursday's stock surge helped the dollar.

"In general, well-performing U.S. asset markets tend to support the dollar, whether it's a background feature or prominent," said Bob Near, a vice president of corporate foreign exchange sales at Bank of New York.

Both the producer price index (PPI) and the core rate -- subtracting food and energy prices -- fell 0.3 percent in May. The headline drop is the fifth in five months, the first time that has occurred since late 1952, the Labor Department said.
Economists had expected both numbers to rise 0.1 percent.
Nevertheless, the dollar's dip below 1.73 marks was a somewhat subdued reaction and traders said the bond market was more likely to focus on the series than the forex market.
"I don't think we're too enthused with PPI in currency markets," Near said.
Dollar/mark opened firmer, quoted at 1.7302/07, compared to 1.7285/95 at Thursday's close. Dollar/yen started at 114.40/45, up from 114.15/25.

Traders said the market was exhausted and the upcoming summits of European Union leaders in Amsterdam starting Monday and of Group of Seven heads of state on June 20-22 may have have offered an excuse for a rest after recent volatility.

But talks on Friday between French and German leaders in Poitiers, France could kick up the dust again if traders detect rancor as differences on the budget stabiliy pact for monetary union are hammered out, dealers said.

German Chancellor Helmut Kohl and Finance Minister Theo Waigel sat down with French Prime Minister Lionel Jospin and Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn. The summit was their first meeting since the new left-wing government took power in France nearly two weeks ago.

Dollar/mark was supported early Friday, after Waigel and Stauss-Kahn said they were cautiously optimistic that the accord to limit budget deficits after the launch of the euro would be agreed to in Amsterdam.
Meanwhile, dollar/yen also saw its range contract overnight, after tumbling then rocketing back up this week.
"The fact is people are getting a little scared to jump in after moving four and a half percent in one night (Thursday)," said a trader at a European bank.
In Tokyo, dollar/yen sagged after Japan reported a larger than expected jump in its Gross Domestic Product (GDP).
Japan's GDP rose a real 1.6 percent in the January through March quarter from the previous quarter, compared to forecasts for a 1.1 percent rise.
Dollar/yen sagged to 113.85 after the news before heading back up to around 114.90.
Elsewhere, the dollar eased to 1.4415/20 Swiss francs from 1.4435/45 and to Canadian $1.3825/30 from C$1.3834/39.
The pound rose to $1.6348/58 from $1.6300/10.
The Australian dollar fell to $0.7517/22 from $0.7525/30.
((--Alden Bentley, 212 859 1667))
